problem: Prior VLN models rely on whole-image visual features and instruction language features, so they do not explicitly ground the places and landmark objects mentioned in the instruction to what appears in the images.
motivation: Instructions refer to key places and landmark objects, so detecting them in the views and aligning them with instruction entities should improve grounding. Agents also need a way to check whether they are actually making progress toward the goal, in order to raise the success rate.
key_idea: Add detected landmark objects and places from the images as extra inputs, link them to instruction entities and image regions through a context-based attention mechanism, and add a progress checker module that verifies real progress toward the goal.
insight: Abstract only: the paper claims that explicit landmark and place detection, context-aware attention, and a progress checker improve R2R performance. No ablations or numbers are available to check which component contributes most.
method: Landmark/place detection: detects the main places and landmark objects mentioned in the instruction within the input images and uses them as extra features alongside whole-image features.
Language and visual encoding: encodes the language features of the natural-language instruction and the visual features of the whole input image.
Context-based attention: an attention mechanism that strengthens the associations among instruction entities, image regions of interest, and detected objects and places.
Progress checker: a module that checks whether the agent is truly approaching the goal, in order to increase the goal-reaching success rate.
